description: This study assesses how robust Lyon's multimodal public transport system is when the electricity supply fails, a growing concern as transport electrifies. Nicolas da Silva Fradique, Angelo Furno and co-authors from Université Gustave Eiffel, Université Grenoble Alpes and ENTPE published it in Transportation Research Record in 2025. A graph-theory framework represents the structure of mobility services and their travel times, links transit lines to their power supply, and combines topological analysis with analysis weighted by observed travel demand. Performance is measured by average travel time, a global efficiency view, and node betweenness centrality, which shows station importance; the two metrics diverge in informative ways. Applied to real Lyon data, the framework identifies metro line D as critical and central, which argues for targeted maintenance and emergency preparedness. Coverage: the Lyon metropolitan public transport network. Access: journal article behind a paywall; the abstract is public. Licence and cost: publisher copyright, paid access. Caveats: static graph analysis without operational rerouting, and power supply mapping is simplified. It supports cascading failure and resilience analysis of electrified transit. It relates to the French national transport data access point, a source of network data, and to the London rail flood-power dependency case study in the catalogue.
